Magnolia second. It is the weakest single-day reading of any shop and I have now recorded that its recovery has reversed. I would walk it this week rather than read it again. Then the exports. Transfers and purchase orders have been frozen since 18 September, so I cannot see a single delivery — nothing I can do from here fixes that; somebody has to import them. And the standing repair: no product in any shop has a low-stock level, so a shelf is only ever visible to me once it has already hit zero. Say the word and I will draft levels for the twenty fastest lines for you to approve.

reading.caveat: The stock side cannot be trusted as read: 2,180 counts are below zero, the lowest at -78,291, and a count below zero is a broken record rather than an empty shelf — so a line shown as out of stock may simply be miscounted, and none of those quantities can be added up. Nobody has set a low-stock level on any product either, so a line is only ever seen the day it crosses to zero. On the sales side, product comparisons can't rank 122 of 500 lines: 66 sold in the earlier week and not this one, 44 are new, 12 had nothing to compare against. Purchase orders and transfers haven't moved since 18 September, so deliveries are invisible; vending stock is 47 days stale.
reading.next:
Greenhills first. Ask the manager what changed in the mall or the roster after 13 September, and count the kiamoy shelf by hand. A hand count is the only way to know: the stock record has too many counts below zero to answer it.

Magnolia second. It was the weakest shop yesterday against the same weekday, and it is down again on the week: two readings pointing the same way. I'd rather look this week than after a third.

Then the shelf. Dikiam fell by half at Greenhills, the same too-thin-to-serve pattern I recorded a week ago. Say the word and I'll draft the AJI BARN order for the kiamoy and dikiam lines; nothing is sent until you send it.

The one structural fix. Set low-stock levels and clear the negative counts. Until both are done I can only tell you a line has already gone, never that it is about to.

So this is not a slow leak across the week. It is one weak Saturday on top of a slightly thin week, which makes it a footfall question before it is a product one.

children.say: Greenhills gave back the most, {gh}{gh.change}, then Magnolia and Shangri-La. OPUS slipped a little on the biggest base. Rockwell grew; North Edsa and Fairview held.
Turn the window to the month and it is a different page: that one is Rockwell's August, not this week.

children.head: Greenhills is the one I can't explain

children.say: It rang {ghtills} tills against {ghtills.was}{ghtills.change}, while its basket stayed within a peso ({ghbasket}). Fewer people, not smaller baskets.
A shop that loses tills on a Monday, a Tuesday and a Saturday alike has not had one bad day. That is footfall or opening hours, and nothing in the sales data can tell those two apart.
The kiamoy money moved rather than left. Kiamoy White nearly stopped selling while king seedless and the premium pack rose in the same week: a deliberate switch, or a relabel nobody told us about.
At Greenhills it is sharper: Kiamoy White all but vanished from the till, and Dikiam fell by half.

scenes.question: how are our stores?
scenes.answer:
The shops are **fine, and the week-on-week headline is one Monday.**

Six of seven days beat the same day a week earlier. The one that did not is a Monday, against a Monday that took nearly double what a Monday takes here - nothing here says why. What separates the shops is what a visit is worth: Fairview grew basket on fewer people, Greenhills the opposite.

Shall I set a watch on Greenhills' basket, so it only speaks if it keeps going?
